summary: The key revision is active II mkawt- alongside inherited Detransitive mikawt-. Repeated plural human agents and -nne objects in JTM and Lahdo outweigh the readers’ instruction to retain a Detransitive-only filing merely because the entry lacked active examples.

JTM 1.1/50 reduces four containers to one; Lahdo The ḥalile/1 explicitly reduces the juice to half. Half-cooking in the edition therefore does not establish a fixed concentration ratio. The inherited Detransitive gloss is retained pending editorial clarification.
Infinitiv kəwoto at JTM 1.1/50 is the process during which clarification occurs. Lahdo kewoto before kәmkawtәnanne may be a cognate process noun; it is not used as proof of a separate voice.
Existing 94/135 has juice as subject of komikawti and 94/137 has a resulting Part. Pass. mkawte. These remain Detransitive sense 1 and are not duplicated.

The permitted kyt/kwy lookups do not fit these finite culinary constructions: kyt has kayət/koyət with stunted growth, and kwy has kwele/kowe cauterising. Their semantic histories do not replace the directly attested kwt cooking series.
Confirm the active/Detransitive contrast in the recordings, especially mkawtina-nne versus mikawti. The active filing follows overt subject/object morphology and is machine-proposed.
Is Lahdo kewoto an Infinitiv/cognate process noun or a standalone lexical noun? The box is supported independently by JTM 1.1/50.
Does the inherited halb gekocht werden refer to partial cooking or reduction of volume? Do not replace the inherited wording until the editors establish the distinction.
The supplied active base forms are incomplete: the entry gives mkawət/mikawət rather than an attested active Preterit/Infectum pair. Obtain a confirmed active Preterit; none is reconstructed here.
